A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TokenSelect. All 15 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original benchmark evaluations, ablations, latency measurements, and extended-context retrieval results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a prefill-latency comparison in Appendix D, Table 6.

M1.justification: Token-level selection, per-head soft voting, chunk-wise prefill selection, the decode Selection Cache, and paged kernels are unchanged. Equations 8–10 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same InfiniteBench tasks, RULER, English LongBench tasks, and extended R.PK/R.KV retrieval up to 2M tokens. The added latency sweep does not introduce a new data domain or task.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds MInference and FlashAttention-2, both implemented in vLLM, as explicit prefill-latency comparators. v1's timing comparisons used InfLLM and FlashInfer-based full attention; MInference already participated in the retained accuracy comparison in Table 3.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D experiment measures end-to-end prefill latency on Llama-3-8B with paged KV management, one A100, and input lengths from 1K to 300K. Existing benchmark metrics and token budgets are retained; the newly stated cache threshold does not establish a change to earlier settings.

E4.justification: Table 4 revises the selection-function ablation by removing Math.F and adding R.PK, where all three selection functions score 100.00. The token-budget and cache-threshold analyses remain, with some token-budget results revised.

E5.justification: Both versions specify greedy decoding without reporting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing cosine-similarity distributions remain unchanged, and the new latency table adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Selected InfiniteBench scores change in Tables 1 and 3–5: Qwen2 En.MC changes from 48.47 to 54.31 and Math.F from 32.57 to 21.71; Llama-3 En.QA changes from 19.39 to 21.32, En.Dia from 14.50 to 8.00, and R.KV from 40.00 to 48.40. Table 5 also revises 1K-token Math.F from 24.57 to 21.71. New Table 6 reports latency and out-of-memory results, including 128K times of 18.827 seconds for MInference and 15.920 for TokenSelect. RULER, LongBench, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Lemma 1, and its complete Appendix A proof retain the same assumptions and mathematical reasoning. Replacing softmax with the symbol sigma and reformatting equations do not change their substance.

C1.justification: v2 removes the explicit model-agnostic claim from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The central training-free inference and length-extrapolation contributions, including the headline 23.84x attention and 2.28x end-to-end speedups, remain.

C2.justification: New Section 8 explains dependence on underlying model quality, possible need for training to address inherited failures, compatibility with long-context post-training, and continuing computational costs. This extends the existing task-specific failure discussion into broader applicability limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, specifies Selection Cache theta = 0.9 for InfiniteBench and LongBench, and provides additional hardware and runtime information. These are new disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments. Conversely, Figure 2's caption loses its Qwen2-7B-Instruct/GovReport provenance.

R1.justification: v2 removes the RepoCoder and CodeFuse-13B references and their introductory application example. It softens the blanket criticism of existing deployment methods and acknowledges MInference's practical adoption. The principal related-work coverage and positioning remain.

P1.justification: Local wording edits, author/front-matter changes, and author-year citations accompany a limited reorganization. Baseline and dataset descriptions move from Section 6.1 into Appendices B/C, while the main narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively retypeset, with a compact author block, different typography, removed running headers, and widespread figure/table repositioning. Table captions move below tables, Table 4 changes a column, and the latency table is added. The nine figure graphics themselves remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The direct MInference timing comparison, code pointer, disclosed cache threshold, and specific limitations modestly improve empirical support and reproducibility. A new reporting defect limits this gain: v2 Table 1 reports a Llama-3 TokenSelect average of 43.90 although its nine scores average approximately 44.84; v1's reported 44.41 was consistent. The added evidence and transparency outweigh this limited defect.
